summary: Ramon Prats works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).

Ran Mao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at Hainan University (BA 1999–2003, MA 2005–2008) and Kasetsart University (PhD 2020), and taught Chinese and other subjects at Hainan University, KU Leuven, and Guizhou University of Finance and Economics.
Randall Studstill specializes in religious studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Richard Payne and teacher Steven D. Goodman.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff, and held professorships at the City University of Hong Kong and Beijing Normal University.

Rangama Chandawimala works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and became an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under masters including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught prominent students such as Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranjeet Kumar Verma works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow and held a scholar post at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad in 2025.
Rano Hodžiakbarovna Guljamova (1940–1985) was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from circa 1957 to 1962 and taught there from 1962 until 1985.
Ranu Kunwar pursued PhD studies at Australian National University from 2022 to 2026 under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron.

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017) and at Santa Clara University (attested 2012).

Raoul Curiel (1913–2000) was a scholar in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and others. He served with the DAFA, directed Pakistan's Department of Archaeology and Museums, and curated coins at the Cabinet des Médailles.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist. He studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (circa 1821–1825), and later taught Georg Bühler.

Raphael Marozzi (1913–1999) was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned a BA from the University of Washington (completed by 1949) and an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (circa 1949–1952).

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at the Moscow Conservatory, Jena, and Heidelberg. He joined the University of Tokyo in 1893, where he taught Hajime Tanabe and Masaharu Anesaki.

Raphaël Voix is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Hamburg, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Rashmi Yadav specializes in Indology. She earned an MSc from Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, studied at Chaudhary Charan Singh University and taught Vedic Mathematics there in 2021, and pursued a PhD at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University in 2022.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College under Ramchandra Dattatraya Ranade. He served as Professor of Samskrta and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith and was president of the Gujarati Sahitya Parishad.

Rasmus Nyerup (1759–1829) was an Indologist who earned an MA at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1784–1803) and served as Chief Librarian at the University of Copenhagen from 1796 to 1829.

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a Danish scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Copenhagen, he held several posts there, including professor of literary history and chair of Oriental Languages.
